open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: “never reused within that history” and “A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number”
open_points.question: Is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the currently restored store history, or must the model also identify the store history so entries with the same sequence number in different pre-loss and post-restore histories are distinguishable?
options: The sequence number is unique only within the current store history, and no history identity is recorded.
AuditEntry identity is the pair of a store-history identity and the sequence number.
AuditEntry receives another stable identity independent of its sequence number.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as identity scoped to the current store history; the lost branch is outside the restored store and has no recorded history identity.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure cardinality and identity scope
open_points.text: “there is at most one” and “Durable, at most one per instance” contradict “A store restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history without it” and R0-89's statement that “the import may then be made again”
open_points.question: Is the one-closure and one-successful-import limit per Registry instance across all restores, or per store history, allowing the same instance to acquire another MigrationClosure after restoration to a pre-import backup?
options: At most one closure per store history; the same instance may have another successful import in a later restored history.
At most one closure per instance across all histories, so restoration must preserve external knowledge that the import already succeeded.
A restored store is considered a new instance for MigrationClosure identity and cardinality.
open_points.default_guess: Scope the closure and the one-successful-import limit to the current store history, allowing another closure after a pre-import restore.
